claims.text: The base alloy is equiatomic HfNbTaTiZr, corresponding to approximately 20 at.% of each element.
The alloy is in the as-cast state.
As-cast equiatomic HfNbTaTiZr has 8–16% room-temperature tensile ductility.
As-cast equiatomic HfNbTaTiZr has a yield strength of 163–530 MPa at 1000 °C.
Poor oxygen resistance limits the use of HfNbTaTiZr in high-temperature air.
Anti-oxidation coatings or further composition modification are required for this refractory high-entropy-alloy family to be used at high temperature in air.
Pack cementation or physical vapor deposition can provide a thin Al-rich surface layer on HfNbTaTiZr.
The aluminized surface will form a continuous alumina scale during high-temperature oxidation.
The resulting alumina scale will be adherent and self-healing.
The alumina scale will significantly retard oxygen ingress into the bulk alloy.
Retarding oxygen ingress will minimize internal oxidation.
Minimizing oxygen ingress and internal oxidation will preserve the alloy's ductility and strength.

After exposure at approximately 1000 °C in an oxygen-rich atmosphere for 10 hours, aluminized specimens will have reduced oxide-scale thickness and diminished oxygen penetration relative to untreated specimens.
After oxidation exposure, the aluminized alloy will retain 8–16% room-temperature tensile ductility.
After oxidation exposure, the aluminized alloy will retain a yield strength of 163–530 MPa at 1000 °C when tested at strain rates of 10⁻⁴–10⁻² s⁻¹.
Thermal-mechanical cycling may cause long-term alumina-scale spallation, and coating thickness may affect the balance between oxidation resistance and mechanical performance.
